headline: High: open-webui’s broad network/MCP/file access can leak or misroute data when paired with taipy, while shared-state and output-trust risks remain plausible but undocumented.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: open-webui can ingest files, browser content, and MCP/tool outputs by default, so attacker-controlled content can reach its prompt context. taipy has no documented ingestion defenses or isolation, so if its outputs are fed into open-webui workflows, prompt injection is plausible. The pairwise bridge is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF taipy outputs are copied into open-webui chats or files
IF open-webui MCP/tool outputs are treated as instructions
mitigations: Disable or restrict MCP/tool connectors in open-webui
Use a separate workspace for taipy-generated artifacts
Add a manual review step before pasting taipy output into open-webui
Strip instructions from imported documents
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for tool/file content

B_data_leakage.rationale: open-webui explicitly handles API keys, files, persistent memory, and broad network egress, while taipy exposes no compensating data controls. If they share a workspace or the same operator account, sensitive prompts or files can flow into open-webui and then out through its APIs/search connectors. The interaction is not directly evidenced, so uncertainty is escalated.
conditions: IF open-webui and taipy share files, notes, or a mounted volume
IF open-webui connectors are enabled for external APIs or search
IF taipy processes sensitive datasets that are later opened in open-webui
mitigations: Keep taipy data in a separate directory from open-webui
Disable external connectors in open-webui for sensitive sessions
Rotate any API keys exposed to open-webui
Limit open-webui to local-only mode
requires-engineering: enforce per-app storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: open-webui has broad network egress and file access, while taipy is documented only as non-egress and runnable=false, so direct write contention is not clearly present. A conflict would require both to mutate the same shared resource, which is not documented here. Because the overlap is uncertain, the lower severity is chosen only for the plausible shared-resource case.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same local files or mounted volume
IF taipy is deployed in a mode that mutates shared state
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Make shared files read-only for one agent
Serialize writes with a simple operator checklist
Use timestamped filenames to avoid collisions
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: open-webui can present tool and document outputs as chat content, and taipy is a data-engineering/automation tool that may consume upstream outputs. If taipy treats open-webui-generated text as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream work products. No verification or provenance controls are documented for either agent, so the pathway is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF taipy ingests open-webui-generated text without validation
IF open-webui outputs are used as source data for taipy pipelines
mitigations: Require human review of open-webui outputs before taipy ingestion
Add schema validation to taipy inputs
Mark open-webui content as untrusted by default
Compare outputs against a second source
requires-engineering: add provenance checks between the agents

E_compliance.rationale: open-webui touches API keys, usage analytics, and persistent memory, while taipy’s profile shows no data classes or residency constraints. That creates a possible compliance mismatch if regulated data is routed through open-webui, but the pairwise violation is not documented and taipy itself shows no conflicting residency policy. The other agent is cited because the risk is about the pair’s data flow.
conditions: IF regulated data is entered into open-webui
IF taipy workflows export data to jurisdictions or services disallowed by policy
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to open-webui
Review retention settings before use
Disable analytics where possible
Document the data flow for taipy jobs
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
